note: The queue behind the in-app new-message banner: what shows, what waits and when the visible banner's timer starts over, for the items a host feeds in (the engine's `notification.present` with surface `inApp`) and the clears it forwards (`notification.clear`). The four kits run this table against their own presenter (Vue createFlareInAppNotifications, Flutter FlareInAppNotifications, SwiftUI FlareInAppNotifications, Compose FlareInAppNotifications); InAppNotificationHost draws what the presenter shows and owns the timer. Items are written `<collapseId>/<body>`.

rules.present: Nothing showing: the item shows at once. The visible banner has the same collapse id: the item replaces it in place. A waiting item has the same collapse id: the item replaces it where it waits. Otherwise the item waits at the end; beyond pendingLimit waiting items the oldest waiting one is dropped, so the newest win.
rules.dismiss: The visible banner goes and the first waiting item shows; with nothing waiting nothing shows.
rules.clear: Waiting items with the given collapse ids go, and when the visible banner has one of them it goes as dismiss says. No ids, nothing goes.
rules.clearAll: Everything goes: the visible banner and every waiting item (the engine's notification.clear with all).
rules.restart: true when the step showed a banner or replaced the visible one: the host starts the visible banner's durationMs over. The timer also stops while the banner is touched, hovered or focused and starts over when that ends.

cases.name: a newer item of the same conversation replaces the visible banner in place
beyond the limit the oldest waiting item is dropped
a waiting item is refreshed where it waits
dismiss shows the next waiting item
clear takes the named conversations away
